findings.evidence: t=(p*2.2+seeded(i,23))%1 resets each particle between radius 3.3 and 1.1. At the first reset for all 20 particles × 3 conditions, p±1e-7 positions differ by 2.199999032 units. findings.location: PBP2 cleft construction lines 180–192; substrate advance and transpeptidation lines 388–426
findings.evidence: At p=.69 first donor D-Ala4 is (0,1.94,.3), but the PBP2 catalytic marker is (1.501406,1.803177,-.184). Donor-to-marker distance is 1.583413 and exact nearest-triangle-surface distance to the PBP2 cleft is 1.048551. At p=.82 the second donor is (1.36,1.94,.3), still .477390 from the nearest PBP2 triangle. Donor sphere radius is only .064; both crosslinks appear while substrates are detached from the drawn catalytic protein.
findings.whyWrong: The lesson specifically shows PBP2 catalyzing these reactions, but neither reacting stem visits its depicted catalytic cleft. Correct bond identity/count cannot substitute for enzyme–substrate contact and therefore the geometry depicts catalysis at a distance.
findings.fix: Continuously position the catalytic PBP2 domain and/or flexible substrate stems so each terminal D-Ala cleavage and crosslink event takes place at the actual drawn active site. Preserve covalent glycan/stem/lipid continuity and existing acceptor occupancy; keep the membrane anchor attached while the domain moves.
findings.verification: For both sequential reactions, test the actual reacting stem atoms/markers against the real active-site marker and local cleft geometry before bond change; require contact-scale distances, correct timing, continuous movement, and preservation of all old molecular conservation invariants. Confirm blocked branch does not cleave or crosslink.

findings.location: beta-lactam ring/carbonyl/covalent geometry lines 333–359 and drugBonds[3] visibility at line 437
findings.evidence: The explicitly constructed carbonyl substituent is at ring corner (+.12,+.12), but acylation removes edge 3 joining (-.12,+.12) to (-.12,-.12), which is not incident on that carbonyl. The covalent segment ends at the ring center, not any ring atom; at p=1 its drug-side endpoint is (1.68,1.8,.25), .169706 from the carbonyl corner (1.8,1.92,.25). Both carbonyl-incident ring edges remain drawn.
findings.whyWrong: Serine-PBP beta-lactam acylation opens the cyclic amide at the carbonyl C–N bond and connects the enzyme to that carbonyl carbon. The current geometry breaks an unrelated edge and draws a purported covalent bond into the empty middle of the ring, contradicting the claimed stable covalent complex.
findings.fix: Explicitly identify the ring carbonyl carbon and adjacent nitrogen in the owned schematic, open their connecting bond, and connect the enzyme active-site serine marker to the same carbonyl carbon. Derive bond endpoints from actual moving objects and preserve the inhibited-state mechanism.
findings.verification: Inspect actual world-space ring/bond endpoints: the cleaved edge must be incident on the marked carbonyl and adjacent nitrogen; covalent bond must end at that carbonyl and the enzyme residue; no detached endpoint in the center and no intact C–N edge after acylation. Test approach, reaction seam and terminal inhibited state.
